headline: AI Test Automation ROI framework to quantify value for finance teams
summary: Traditional ROI formulas fall short for AI-powered testing. This guide offers a new framework to capture compounding returns and business value.
details: QA leaders often struggle to quantify the return on investment for test automation, especially with the rise of AI-powered tools. Traditional ROI calculations, designed for scripted automation, fail to capture the unique benefits of AI test generation, self-healing scripts, and intelligent failure triage.

The cost of maintaining traditional automation scripts can consume 30-40% of engineering time. AI's self-healing capabilities significantly reduce this burden, offering a value stream that traditional formulas miss. This framework accounts for hours saved not just from manual testing, but also from reduced maintenance.

AI test automation also enhances bug detection and triage. Intelligent failure classification and AI-generated test cases can catch defects that would otherwise reach production, preventing costly fixes and reputational damage. The article highlights that the cost of poor software quality in the US has reached an estimated $2.41 trillion.

Furthermore, AI test automation enables faster shipping with increased confidence. By reducing sprint testing overhead, teams can redirect capacity to new feature development, unlocking significant business value. For example, a 20% reduction in testing overhead can recover substantial engineering hours annually.

Unlike traditional automation's linear returns, AI systems learn and improve over time, delivering compounding returns. This new framework measures four categories of return: updated traditional savings, defect prevention, faster shipping, and recovered capacity, providing a comprehensive business case for AI test automation investments.

headline: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super Beats GPT on Coding Benchmark by 20 Points
summary: NVIDIA's new open-weight AI model achieves 60.47% on SWE-Bench Verified, outperforming GPT-OSS-120B and offering 2.2x inference throughput.
details: NVIDIA has unveiled Nemotron 3 Super, a 120-billion-parameter open-weight AI model that has set a new standard on the SWE-Bench Verified coding benchmark. Scoring 60.47%, it significantly surpasses GPT-OSS-120B's 41.90%, demonstrating a nearly 20-point lead in rigorous coding task evaluation.

This hybrid model is NVIDIA's first designed for agentic AI workloads, capable of multi-step reasoning, long-document comprehension, and complex goal completion. It integrates Mamba-2 layers for efficient long-context processing (up to 1M tokens) and standard transformer layers for precise attention-based reasoning, offering the strengths of both without their drawbacks.

Nemotron 3 Super also features LatentMoE for expert routing and Multi-Token Prediction for speculative decoding. LatentMoE activates more specialized sub-networks per token at no extra computational cost, leading to richer outputs. MTP predicts and verifies multiple tokens simultaneously, achieving up to 3x speedup in wall-clock time.

The model's performance on SWE-Bench Verified is particularly noteworthy, as it directly measures the ability to resolve real GitHub issues, a crucial task for production agentic coding systems. Its 60.47% score indicates a substantial improvement in reliably navigating and fixing code at scale.

Furthermore, Nemotron 3 Super demonstrates exceptional long-context coherence, scoring 91.75% on the RULER benchmark at 1 million tokens, compared to GPT-OSS-120B's 22.30%. This capability is vital for AI systems that need to process and understand entire code repositories.

Nemotron 3 Super is available for free on OpenRouter and Hugging Face, and for enterprise deployment via NVIDIA NIM containers, making advanced open-weight AI more accessible to developers and businesses.
